lessons.title: Language Exchange
lessons.subtitle: Learn 語言 and 交換.

steps.explanation: 語言 means language.
交換 means exchange.

lessons.title: So Enthusiastic
lessons.subtitle: Learn 熱心, 西班牙文, and the degree use of 那麼.

steps.explanation: 熱心 describes enthusiasm/helpfulness.
西班牙文 is Spanish.

steps.prompt: In 你那麼熱心, 那麼 means…
steps.explanation: Here 那麼 means 'so / that' before a degree description, not 'then / in that case'.

steps.audioText: 你那麼熱心教我西班牙文。
steps.explanation: The example uses 西班牙文.

lessons.title: No Need to Be So Polite
lessons.subtitle: Learn 一樣 and the politeness expressions.

steps.prompt: 不必客氣 is closest to…
options: No need to be so polite / Don't mention it.
steps.answer: No need to be so polite / Don't mention it.
steps.explanation: It is a fixed politeness response.
太客氣 reacts to someone's courtesy.
Here 一樣 means 'the same / likewise'.

steps.prompt: In 過生日, 過 means…
steps.explanation: In 過生日, 過 means 'celebrate'.
過生日 is the natural expression for celebrating a birthday.

lessons.title: As Soon As…
lessons.subtitle: Use 一…就… for an immediate sequence.

options: Subject + 一 + Event A，(Subject) + 就 + Event B
Subject + 就 + Event A，一 + Event B
一 + Subject + 就 + Event A
steps.answer: Subject + 一 + Event A，(Subject) + 就 + Event B
steps.explanation: 一 marks Event A; 就 marks Event B.

steps.prompt: If the subject is the same in both events…
options: the repeated second subject may be omitted
steps.answer: the repeated second subject may be omitted
steps.explanation: The pattern allows omission of the repeated subject.

options: Either Event A or Event B can be negative.
Only Event B can be negative.
steps.answer: Either Event A or Event B can be negative.
steps.explanation: The pattern permits both.

steps.prompt: How can you form a yes/no question with 一…就…?
options: Use 嗎 or 是不是.
steps.answer: Use 嗎 or 是不是.
steps.explanation: Use 嗎 or 是不是; ordinary A-not-A is unavailable in this pattern.

lessons.title: Around Five at the Gate
lessons.subtitle: Use 左右 after a time and 門口 for an entrance.

steps.prompt: Where does 左右 go in 五點左右?
steps.explanation: 左右 follows the estimate.
門口 is an entrance.
左右 follows the complete time expression.

lessons.title: Unit 38 Review
lessons.subtitle: Retrieve the appointment vocabulary, seven new characters, and 一…就….

steps.audioText: 語言交換的時候，你那麼熱心。
steps.explanation: 語言交換 means language exchange.
The audio says 不必客氣.
The speaker waits at the school entrance.
熱心 means enthusiastic/warm-hearted.
西班牙文 is the language.
一樣 means 'same; alike'.

steps.prompt: In 過生日, 過 means…
steps.explanation: In 過生日, 過 means 'celebrate'.
太客氣 reacts to someone's kindness.

steps.prompt: What marks the first event in 一…就…?
steps.explanation: 一 precedes Event A.

steps.prompt: What marks the immediately following event?
steps.explanation: 就 precedes Event B.
一沒人 is negative Event A.

steps.prompt: Which statement about 一…就… questions is accurate?
options: Use 嗎 or 是不是; ordinary A-not-A is unavailable.
steps.answer: Use 嗎 or 是不是; ordinary A-not-A is unavailable.
steps.explanation: Both 嗎 and 是不是 are valid here; ordinary A-not-A is not.

steps.prompt: Class ends and you immediately go meet a friend. Which fits?
steps.explanation: 一…就… expresses immediate sequence.
左右 follows the time.

交.note: 交 appears in 交換 jiāohuàn, “exchange.” Learn the two-character word as a unit.
交.memory: A dot and horizontal sit over two small strokes and a wide crossing pair. The crossing shape is a visual cue for exchange.

parts.label: 交
parts.name: crossing form
parts.description: A dot and horizontal sit over two small strokes and a wide crossing pair. The crossing shape is a visual cue for exchange.

換.note: 換 means “change; exchange.” 交換 jiāohuàn means to exchange something with someone.
換.memory: A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: Hand component in 換: strokes 1–3. A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

parts.label: 奐
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 換: strokes 4–12. A hand 扌 stands beside 奐. Use the hand as a cue for changing or exchanging something.

牙.note: 牙 means “tooth” on its own. In 西班牙文, it is part of the name for Spanish; do not translate that name character by character.
牙.memory: Notice the angular top, the long hooked stroke, and the final slant crossing down to the left.

parts.label: 牙
parts.name: tooth form
parts.description: Notice the angular top, the long hooked stroke, and the final slant crossing down to the left.

必.note: 必 relates to necessity. 不必 in 不必客氣 means “there is no need to”; the phrase means “You’re welcome / don’t mention it.”
必.memory: It resembles 心 with an extra diagonal passing through it. Follow the animation: the writing order is not simply 心 plus a final slash.

parts.label: 必
parts.name: crossed-heart form
parts.description: It resembles 心 with an extra diagonal passing through it. Follow the animation: the writing order is not simply 心 plus a final slash.

example.meaning: no need to be so polite

氣.meaning: air; manner; component of 客氣
氣.note: 氣 means “air; breath,” but 客氣 kèqì is a whole word about politeness. 不必客氣 is a polite response to thanks.
氣.memory: The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

parts.label: 气
parts.name: outer component
parts.description: Outer component in 氣: strokes 1–4. The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

parts.label: 米
parts.name: inner component
parts.description: Inner component in 氣: strokes 5–10. The sweeping 气 encloses 米. Leave room for the rice-like lower strokes beneath the top.

氣.partOrderLabel: outer frame first, then the inside

門.note: 門 mén means “door; gate.” 門口 ménkǒu is the entrance or doorway.
門.memory: Picture two tall door panels facing each other, with an opening between them. Write the left panel before the right.

parts.label: 門
parts.name: paired door panels
parts.description: Picture two tall door panels facing each other, with an opening between them. Write the left panel before the right.

口.note: You have seen 口 inside other characters. Now write it on its own. In 路口 it refers to an opening or junction.
口.memory: Remember 口 as a three-stroke box: left edge, top-and-right bend, then the bottom closes it.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: whole character
parts.description: 口 is a single component. Its top and right edges are written together as one bent stroke.

u38-yi-jiu.title: As soon as… with 一…就…
u38-yi-jiu.pattern: Subject + 一 + Event A，(Subject) + 就 + Event B
u38-yi-jiu.explanation: 一…就… links two events when Event B follows Event A immediately. 一 comes before Event A and 就 before Event B; both follow the subject. If the subject is the same, the repeated subject may be omitted. Either event can be affirmative or negative. The rule here does not use ordinary A-not-A inside this construction; yes/no questions can use 嗎 or 是不是. Both question strategies are valid.

examples.meaning: As soon as class ends, I come back.

examples.pinyin: Nàlǐ yì méi rén, wǒ jiù huí jiā.
examples.meaning: As soon as nobody is there, I go home.

examples.text: 老闆今天早上一到公司，就不開心。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn jīntiān zǎoshang yí dào gōngsī, jiù bù kāixīn.
examples.meaning: As soon as the boss got to the company this morning, he was unhappy.

u38-yi-jiu.remember: 一 before Event A; 就 before the immediate Event B. Same subject may be omitted. Either event may be negative; ask with 嗎 or 是不是, not ordinary A-not-A.
